title: Learning When to Update: A Near-Optimal Timing Bandit Approach
abstract: arXiv:2609.37932v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Systems operating in dynamic environments require timely updates to sustain performance. For resource-intensive systems such as machine learning models and digital twins, strategically timing updates is essential. Updating too frequently wastes resources, while updating too infrequently leads to costly performance degradation. The problem is particularly challenging when the system's degradation pattern is unknown a priori, as is common in new operating environments. We formalize this challenge as a novel \emph{timing bandit} problem, where each arm represents a candidate update interval with a fixed update cost and an unknown, stochastic degradation cost. Three structural properties distinguish this setting from standard multi-armed bandits: selecting an interval commits the learner to multiple time slots before the next update; arm costs are composed of per-step degradation costs and a fixed update cost; and selecting a longer interval

translated_title: 学习何时更新：一种近最优的时序老虎机方法
translated_abstract: 在动态环境中运行的系统需要及时更新以维持性能。对于机器学习模型和数字孪生等资源密集型系统而言，策略性地安排更新时机至关重要。更新过于频繁会浪费资源，而更新过于稀疏则会导致代价高昂的性能下降。当系统的退化模式无法先验已知时，这一问题尤为具有挑战性，而这在新运行环境中十分常见。我们将这一挑战形式化为一个新颖的时序老虎机问题，其中每个臂代表一个候选更新间隔，具有固定的更新成本和未知的随机退化成本。有三个结构性特征将该设定与标准多臂老虎机区分开来：选择某个间隔会使学习者在下一次更新之前被锁定于多个时间槽；臂的成本由每步退化成本和固定更新成本共同构成；以及选择更长的间隔……
tldr: 该论文提出了一种新颖的“时序老虎机”问题形式化，用于在系统退化模式先验未知的情况下学习近最优的更新时机。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes a novel "timing bandit" problem to learn near-optimal update timing when the system's degradation pattern is unknown a priori.
